comparison: Both evaluations find strong support for claims C1, C2, C24-26, C30-31, C33 regarding YAP target gene suppression in RNA-seq data. OpenEval additionally addresses the paradoxical elevation (C34-35) which peer reviewers also accept without challenge (R2).

Perfect agreement on claims C4, C36, C38-39. Both find the dual-luciferase reporter assays compelling evidence for LATS-independent YAP inhibition by NSP13. OpenEval notes unresolved concerns about episomal DNA suppression (C40-43), which peer reviewers address separately in R11.

Both strongly support the in vivo findings (C5, C45-46, C49) showing NSP13 improves survival and cardiac function in YAP5SA mice. Peer Reviewer 3 describes the data as 'striking,' matching OpenEval's assessment of appropriate statistical analysis and experimental design.

Strong agreement on claims C6, C52-57 regarding NSP13 mutant and truncation analysis. Both find the reporter assay data convincingly demonstrate that helicase domain activity is required for YAP suppression. OpenEval includes additional claims (C86, C94, C96-97) not explicitly addressed by peer reviewers.

Both support claim C58 regarding variant NSP13 mutants suppressing YAP. OpenEval provides more detailed rationale citing sequence conservation (C50-51), while peer reviewers accept this finding without specific commentary.

Strong agreement on claims C7, C62-65 regarding NSP13-TEAD4 interaction and the platform/scaffold model. Both evaluations find the co-IP data compelling. OpenEval additionally addresses nuclease treatment (C69) and TEAD4-mediated enhancement (C72).

Perfect agreement on claims C59-61, C66-68. Both support the immunofluorescence and co-IP data showing nuclear localization and TEAD4-mediated interaction. Both note that NSP13 stabilization inference (C68) is somewhat speculative but reasonable.

Strong concordance with both evaluations rating these claims as UNCERTAIN. Both acknowledge IP-MS data (C70-71, C75-76) but agree the chromatin remodeling mechanism (C74, C95) is incomplete. Peer Reviewer 3 explicitly states 'requires further study,' matching OpenEval's assessment that additional validation is needed.

Both support claims C40-43 regarding dose-dependent effects and specificity controls. OpenEval additionally addresses C44 (Notch reporter specificity), which peer reviewers evaluate separately in R12, also finding it supported.
Perfect agreement on claim C69. Both find the nuclease treatment experiments convincingly demonstrate direct protein-protein interaction rather than nucleic acid-mediated bridging.

Divergent evaluations of claims C90-91. OpenEval rates as UNCERTAIN, emphasizing the highly speculative nature of therapeutic potential (C91) with no validation data. Peer reviewers rate as SUPPORTED, accepting the mechanistic contribution while acknowledging future studies are needed for therapeutic validation.

OpenEval evaluates claims C78-83 as established background knowledge and context-dependent CCT3 function. Peer reviewers do not provide a separate evaluation of these contextual/background claims, though they accept CCT3 findings in R13.

OpenEval evaluates extensive background claims (C9-23, C27-29, C32, C37, C48, C84-85, C87-89, C93) as appropriately cited established knowledge. Peer reviewers do not separately evaluate background/contextual claims.
Peer reviewers separately evaluate the paradoxical elevation of some YAP targets (C34-35) as supported. OpenEval addresses these claims within R1 as part of the overall RNA-seq analysis.
Peer reviewers provide a focused evaluation on variant analysis (C58) alone. OpenEval addresses this in R5 along with sequence conservation rationale (C50-51).
Peer reviewers separately evaluate Notch reporter specificity control (C44) as supported. OpenEval addresses this claim within R9 alongside other specificity controls (C40-43).
Peer reviewers separately evaluate CCT3 as YAP repressor (C77) as supported. OpenEval addresses this claim within R8 as part of the broader mechanistic evaluation including IP-MS findings.
